**Supplerende indikator: Hjertesvigt efter atrieflimren** (Supplementary indicator: Heart failure after atrial fibrillation) is a clinical metric used within the Danish healthcare system to identify the development of heart failure as a complication following a new diagnosis of atrial fibrillation [^src1]. Its primary significance lies in supporting the evaluation of long-term patient outcomes and the overall quality of treatment [^src1]. 

This indicator is documented as part of the [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] report, which is published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (Regional Clinical Quality Improvement Program) [^src1]. Within the report, it is analyzed alongside other key metrics, such as Indikator 15 (heart failure within one year of a new diagnosis) and Indikator 11 (severe bleeding within one year) [^src1]. The data for this supplementary indicator is presented at the national level and is further stratified by regions, health clusters, and specific cluster areas [^src1]. This granular breakdown allows healthcare administrators and policymakers to compare regional performance, identify variations in clinical practice, and drive quality improvement initiatives across Denmark [^src1].
